newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Komercni, banking shares sour Prague bourse.
newsitem.headline: Komercni, banking shares sour Prague bourse.

text.p: Another poor performance in shares of the largest Czech bank, Komercni Banka a.s., kept key Prague Stock Exchange indices in negative territory on Friday despite minor to moderate gains elsewhere.

A cloudy economic outlook and the drain on the economy from recent flooding in the eastern part of the country continued to drag down the financials, especially Komercni with the country's largest loan portfolio, dealers said.

The Reuters Prague RPIX index of the top 11 shares in the real-time market dropped 2.9 points to 1,032.5, eventhough the two most-capitalised issues, power utility CEZ a.s. and SPT Telecom posted gains.
The broader PX50 index lost 0.5 points to 504.5, and for the week edged up two points from lastFriday's close.

Komercni dropped five crowns at the morning fixing but then fell 55 crowns below Thursday's close in real-time trading to finish the week at 1,640. The bank's shares have fallen steadily since July 3 when it was above the 1,800 level.

"As the economy is not doing extremely well this year it could happen that at the end of the year the quality of (Komercni's) loan portfolio will worsen as well so there will be a need for provisions for covering non-performing loans," Miroslav Nosal, analyst at Patria Finance told Reuters.

He said that the outlook for Komercni's first-half results, expected by the end of this month, was disappointing, and net profit could be about "half a billion crowns lower" than last year's six-month net result of 3.059 billion crowns .
"The outlook (for Komercni)... in not that encouraging," Nosal said.
The largest savings bank Ceska Sporitelna was down five crowns at 275, while the third largest bank IPB fell seven crowns to 230.
A four crown gain to CEZ to 910 and a ten crown rise in SPT Telecom to 3,625 helped stem the market's losses.
Of the 11-shares trading in the real-time market, six posted gains and four losses, while on the broader market, gainers outpaced losers 104 to 81 with 52 issues unchanged.
Turnover was moderate at 632 million crowns on volume of 464,298 shares changing hands.

Dealers said overall trading activity was still dampened by the impact of flooding in the eastern part of the country and forecasts for more rain for the area where production at hundreds of businesses had been shut.
